mechanism_failure_point: Purpose fragmentation across agents and tools
part_1_status: Benign-looking subtasks can compose into a harmful terminal objective.
part_2_status: Planning and tool-use gains expand the feasible workflow.
critical_gap: No end-to-end standard binds local actions to a persistent root purpose.

mechanism_failure_point: Safeguard removal, jailbreaks, and modifiable weights
part_1_status: Default refusals are not stable under adaptive attack or model modification.
part_2_status: Open and frontier variants must be tracked separately by safeguard state.

part_1_status: Target attributes can be separated from content generation and delivery.
part_2_status: Persuasion and profiling capabilities are measurable but not fully outcome-validated.
critical_gap: Organic, proxy, and conversational targeting often falls outside ad rules.

mechanism_failure_point: Multi-turn adaptation, memory, and long-horizon influence
part_1_status: Single-turn safety tests miss cumulative interaction effects.
part_2_status: Memory and agent scaffolds increase adaptation and persistence.

mechanism_failure_point: Synthetic intimacy, affective inference, and dependency
part_1_status: Relational framing can lower resistance without an overtly political request.
part_2_status: Companion-like behavior and personalized trust require separate evaluation.
critical_gap: Current law focuses on acute harm, vulnerability classes, or data—not relational dependence.

mechanism_failure_point: Agentic planning, tools, permissions, and autonomous action
part_1_status: Harm emerges at the workflow level, not only in generated text.
part_2_status: Agent scaffolds expose capabilities hidden by model-only benchmarks.
critical_gap: No generally binding agent authorization and accountability standard.

mechanism_failure_point: False voting information and official-source substitution
part_1_status: Plausible answers can bypass content-centered safeguards.
part_2_status: Retrieval and citation quality vary by language and locale.
critical_gap: Coverage is uneven across assistants, languages, and local elections.

part_1_status: Generation is cheap; authenticity judgments shift to recipients and platforms.
part_2_status: Text, audio, image, and video provenance have different robustness limits.
critical_gap: Provenance is removable and does not address truthful manipulation.

part_1_status: The model can generate content, but distribution determines scale and exposure.
part_2_status: Capability measures must be combined with reach and recommender behavior.
critical_gap: Independent causal evidence and cross-platform exposure measures remain thin.

mechanism_failure_point: Coordinated inauthentic behavior and account networks
part_1_status: Task decomposition enables industrialized but individually low-signal operations.
part_2_status: Agent throughput and cost affect feasible scale.
critical_gap: Evasion through resellers, cross-platform migration, and legitimate activism.

part_1_status: Delivery can be outsourced beyond visible platform surfaces.
part_2_status: Open models and external tools reduce central observability.
critical_gap: Need privacy-preserving exposure and incident indicators.

mechanism_failure_point: Evidence loss, weak attribution, and delayed investigation
part_1_status: Without traces, composite failures cannot be reconstructed.
critical_gap: No shared cross-layer chain-of-custody and retention standard.

mechanism_failure_point: Assistant gatekeeping and answer-layer source concentration
part_1_status: A single synthesized answer obscures selection and omission decisions.
part_2_status: Better models may become a more trusted default interface.
critical_gap: Media and platform law does not yet fully govern generative answer layers.

part_1_status: Delegation moves judgment and operational knowledge outside the institution.
part_2_status: Capability gains increase incentives to substitute rather than augment expertise.
critical_gap: No standard measures lost institutional judgment or decision authority.

mechanism_failure_point: Cross-stack concentration of compute, cloud, models, defaults, and data
part_1_status: Controller power determines which safeguards and evidence are available.
part_2_status: Capability concentration interacts with ownership and distribution.
critical_gap: Market share does not measure delegated decisions or control of information environments.

mechanism_failure_point: Overbroad mitigation, censorship, and state or incumbent capture
part_1_status: Safety classification can be wrong or strategically manipulated.
part_2_status: Centralized evaluation can entrench frontier providers and benchmark monoculture.
critical_gap: Intervention evaluation rarely measures rights cost alongside risk reduction.
